analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia
key_insights: US equities rallied sharply on Monday. S&P 500 +4.73%, Nasdaq +6.51%, Dow +3.01%, the best sessions since 9 April 2025. Breadth was over 5:1 positive, but equal-weight S&P lagged cap-weight by more than 200 bp.

The rebound started as a bounce off Friday's lows led by AI names and accelerated when Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang. NVDA rose 31.5%. The report says the bounce's credibility is debatable given a hawkish-leaning Fed.

Nvidia reinstatement drew upgrades from Oppenheimer (Outperform) and Melius (Buy), Cantor reiterated Overweight and re-added it to Top Picks, and B. Riley called a bottom in the SOX. Overhangs remain: Goldman flagged DOJ/SEC probes, KeyBanc stays Sector Weight, and Huang must still appear before congressional committees.

US November flash composite PMI was 54.6 vs 56.1 consensus and 55.9 in October, the lowest since Jul-26. Services were 54.7 vs 56.4 consensus. Prices cooled but stayed elevated, and supplier delivery times were the longest since Aug-22.

Fed policy-mistake talk is rising after the AI-driven selloff. Waller reiterated a possible 50 bp hike in December and Bessent said the Fed risks overtightening. Strategists still expect the Fed to stay the course and favor curve flatteners with long-end bonds outperforming.

Global crude exports hit a record 47.53M bpd in October per Kpler. WTI settled just above $80 (-3.7%) and Brent is at its lowest since August-end on expectations of talks to end the war. Costs stay high from war insurance premiums and longer routes around Hormuz.

Copper is down nearly 20% from the September peak. UBS attributes it more to the AI trade unwind, hawkish Fed repricing and dollar strength than weaker demand. UBS flags sustained outflows as the key downside risk and stays constructive longer term.

Deal flow: CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler for about $43.9B in stock at a ~34% premium (ZS +17.7%, CRWD -8.9%). Texas Pacific Land will buy Eaglerock Land for $3B in stock. Clariant and CD&R are in talks to buy Ashland for about $3.39B in cash.

European equities closed sharply higher after the steepest weekly drop since March. Tech, industrials and miners led, 16 of 19 sectors rose, and autos lagged after a BNP Paribas Exane downgrade to underweight. The rebound was attributed to contrarian positioning, volatility and sentiment signals.
Eurozone composite flash PMI was steady at 51.7 vs 51.9 consensus. The Germany-France divergence is the widest in six years, with Germany at 55.0 and France at 46.1.

ECB: Simkus said a December hike may not suffice. Markets price 87% odds of a 25 bp hike to a 2.75% deposit rate, about 60 bp more tightening by late 2027, and a peak near 3.10-3.11%. The market is split on a BoE move in December vs February.
UK composite PMI fell to 52.3 vs 52.9 consensus. The UK and EU announced a deal worth up to £17B a year. Macron is weighing a constitutional spending golden rule.

Asia: policy support dominated after last week's rout. China cuts the minimum margin ratio to 80% from 100% on 30-Nov, freeing about CNY400B. Taiwan banned short selling after the Taiex's worst week in 35 years. South Korea is preparing a stabilization fund. Kospi closed -3.3%, its lowest since January.

Trump threatened a tax on US firms building data centers overseas. GS E&C fell 12.6%. Nvidia server partners halted Southeast Asia shipments under new US export controls, and uncertainty is growing for Feynman architecture plans from 2028.

Central banks in Asia: the BOK is expected to hike to 3.25% on 26-Nov and the RBI to hike in December. India fell 1.75% after a stellar month, while foreign investors keep buying India for its lack of AI exposure and selling Seoul.

market_movers.rationale: Board reinstated Huang as CEO and the stock rose 31.5%. Oppenheimer upgraded to Outperform and Melius to Buy, while Goldman flags DOJ/SEC probes and KeyBanc stays at Sector Weight.
Piper Sandler upgraded on expected solid comp growth, margin expansion and improving lower-income consumer spending.
CrowdStrike all-stock offer of about $43.9B at a ~34% premium, expected to close in H2 of CRWD FY28.
Stock fell 8.9% on the Zscaler deal, which management expects to deliver $500M run-rate synergies within 18-24 months.
Phase 2B KT-621 atopic dermatitis trial met all primary and secondary endpoints, stock +30.4%.
New 18-year lease with an investment-grade hyperscaler for 150 MW, stock +20.3%.
CEO Haas seen as a candidate to replace Huang reaffirmed commitment, with an agreement through 2033.
Proposed CMS Medicare Advantage Stars changes seen as likely to reduce industry payments.
Dividend suspended while it evaluates strategic alternatives, stock -11.8%.
Clariant and CD&R in talks for an all-cash deal at a small premium, stock -3.8%.
Deutsche Bank sees strong biosimilars growth and easing China penicillin pressure.
Azelis upgraded by Barclays on improving growth, removal of EQT overhang and deleveraging.
Bankinter upgraded by Oddo on valuation after a ~20% decline, not on sector outperformance.
Marks & Spencer downgraded by UBS on heavy Food capacity investment delaying margin benefits.
Interparfums downgraded by Goldman Sachs after a 65% rise, at 24x forward P/E, with Puig preferred.
Brenntag downgraded by Barclays on FY27 earnings normalisation risk.
Vår Energi upgraded by DNB on 2027 production upside and a 10% dividend yield.
Nemetschek downgraded by JPMorgan on slowing Design subscription migration and a complex HCSS acquisition, at about 20x FY27 earnings.
BNP Paribas Exane downgraded the European autos sector to underweight.
Missouri court approved a Roundup settlement capped at $7.25B over 21 years, reducing litigation uncertainty.
Crest Nicholson guided an FY adjusted operating loss of £30-40M and is in covenant talks with lenders, stock -29.6%.

sector_views.rationale: BNP Paribas Exane downgraded the group to underweight and autos were the weakest sector.
CMS proposed Medicare Advantage Stars changes seen as likely to reduce industry payments.
Semis, memory and neocloud led the rebound, and B. Riley called a bottom in the SOX.

earnings_insights: Julius Baer reported 10M AuM of CHF553B vs consensus CHF555.5B, and 10M net new assets of CHF8.5B vs ZKB estimate CHF10.5B. The stock fell 1.8%.
Drax said 2026 adjusted core profit will exceed company-compiled consensus of £721M, and guided to £800M-£900M in 2029. Stock +5.2%.
Crest Nicholson guided FY adjusted operating loss of £30-40M vs prior guidance of about a £10M loss. The stock fell 29.6%.
Takkt cut 2026 guidance after an October cyberattack. Organic revenue is now forecast at -7% vs prior -7% to +3%, and adjusted EBITDA margin is slightly below 2% vs prior 2-5%.
Zhejiang Leapmotor Q3 revenue missed estimates (-13%). Want Want China H1 revenue was -10% y/y (-15.5%). Unisound Q3 revenue was about CNY344M, +53.3% y/y.
Hongkong Land reported Q3 underlying profit +38% y/y.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Below the 56.1 consensus and the lowest since Jul-26, adding to growth-slowdown concerns.
Unchanged from October and below the 51.9 consensus, with Germany and France diverging.
Two-month low vs 52.9 consensus, with services at 52.0.
A 25 bp hike to 2.75% is nearly fully priced.
Well above the ECB 2% target, supporting hikes.
Down 3.7% on hopes for talks to end the war.
Experts expect a hike, with 3.5% next year.

trade_ideas.description: Curve flattener trades in US Treasuries, with long-end bonds outperforming
trade_ideas.rationale: Strategists expect the Fed to keep hiking and markets to price in the growth impact of rate hikes.

risk_factors: The credibility of the US rebound is questionable given a hawkish Fed and a possible policy mistake.
Regulatory overhangs on Nvidia, including DOJ/SEC probes and congressional appearances.
Further export controls and a slower data center buildout after the midterms.
Sustained copper outflows from US stockpiles.
Fiscal and political uncertainty in France.
Asian market stress, with policy support needed in Korea, Taiwan and China.
vol_and_positioning: The volatility index closed at 26.62, down 25.83% on the day, and is up 37.08% month to date.
Positioning, volatility and sentiment dynamics were cited as contrarian tailwinds for the US and European rebounds.
Taiwan banned short selling below the previous close, the third short-sale move this month, and raised short margin to 150% from 130%.
Foreign selling in Seoul is at a record, while foreign buying of India stocks is also at a record.
Market-implied odds of three Fed hikes by Mar-2027 have fallen amid the volatility.
geopolitical: Trump administration reportedly refrained from renewed attacks after the US midterms, and crude eased on expectations of talks to end the war. Iran had effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz.
New US export controls led Nvidia server partners to halt shipments to Southeast Asia.
Trump threatened a tax on US firms building data centers overseas.
UK and EU announced a joint agreement worth up to £17B a year.
Nvidia reinstatement came amid reports of links between Huang's mistress and China's Ministry of State Security, and the board received input from senior US government levels.
cross_bank_references: Goldman flagged DOJ/SEC probes on Nvidia while KeyBanc maintains Sector Weight.
UBS argued the copper selloff more likely reflects the AI trade unwind than weaker demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Best session since April 2025 with 5:1 breadth, driven by AI names, Nvidia reinstatement and contrarian positioning and sentiment signals.
tension_points.bear_case: Credibility is debatable given a hawkish-leaning Fed, equal-weight lagging by over 200 bp, a softer flash PMI and Nvidia regulatory overhangs.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says the selloff reflects the AI trade unwind, hawkish Fed repricing and dollar strength, not weaker demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Slowing manufacturing momentum, weak China construction data and a below-consensus Philly Fed point to slowing growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS flags sustained copper outflows as the key downside risk.
